tests.name: Haemoglobin
tests.plain_english: Haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
tests.low_means: Low haemoglobin may indicate anaemia, which can cause tiredness and breathlessness.
tests.high_means: High haemoglobin can sometimes indicate dehydration or a blood disorder.

tests.name: White Blood Cell Count
tests.plain_english: White blood cells are part of your immune system and help fight infections.
tests.low_means: A low white cell count may mean your immune system is weakened.
tests.high_means: A high white cell count can indicate infection, inflammation, or in rare cases a blood disorder.

tests.name: Platelets
tests.plain_english: Platelets are tiny blood cells that help your blood clot when you have a cut or injury.
tests.low_means: Low platelets can mean your blood takes longer to clot, increasing bleeding risk.
tests.high_means: High platelets can increase the risk of blood clots.

tests.name: HbA1c
tests.plain_english: HbA1c measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2-3 months. It is used to diagnose and monitor diabetes.
tests.low_means: A very low HbA1c may indicate risk of hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar).
tests.high_means: A high HbA1c indicates your blood sugar has been elevated, which may suggest pre-diabetes or diabetes.

tests.name: Total Cholesterol
tests.plain_english: Cholesterol is a fatty substance in your blood. Some is needed but too much can increase heart disease risk.
tests.low_means: Very low cholesterol is unusual and your GP can advise if this is a concern.
tests.high_means: High cholesterol increases the risk of heart disease and stroke.

tests.name: LDL Cholesterol
tests.plain_english: LDL is often called bad cholesterol. High levels can build up in artery walls and increase heart disease risk.
tests.low_means: Low LDL is generally considered protective for heart health.
tests.high_means: High LDL increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.

tests.name: HDL Cholesterol
tests.plain_english: HDL is often called good cholesterol. It helps remove other forms of cholesterol from your bloodstream.
tests.low_means: Low HDL increases the risk of heart disease.
tests.high_means: High HDL is generally considered protective and desirable.

tests.name: TSH
tests.plain_english: TSH is a hormone produced by your pituitary gland that tells your thyroid how much hormone to make.
tests.low_means: Low TSH may indicate an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism).
tests.high_means: High TSH may indicate an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism).

tests.name: Ferritin
tests.plain_english: Ferritin is a protein that stores iron in your body. It is a good indicator of your iron levels.
tests.low_means: Low ferritin indicates low iron stores, which can lead to iron deficiency anaemia.
tests.high_means: High ferritin can indicate inflammation, liver disease, or iron overload.

tests.name: Vitamin D
tests.plain_english: Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium and is essential for healthy bones, teeth, and muscles.
tests.low_means: Low vitamin D (deficiency) can cause bone pain, muscle weakness, and fatigue.
tests.high_means: Very high vitamin D from excessive supplements can be harmful.

tests.name: Vitamin B12
tests.plain_english: Vitamin B12 is essential for making red blood cells and keeping your nervous system healthy.
tests.low_means: Low B12 can cause anaemia, fatigue, and neurological symptoms.
tests.high_means: Very high B12 may indicate liver disease or certain blood conditions.

tests.name: Creatinine
tests.plain_english: Creatinine is a waste product filtered by your kidneys. It is used to assess kidney function.
tests.low_means: Low creatinine can indicate low muscle mass.
tests.high_means: High creatinine may indicate that your kidneys are not filtering waste effectively.

tests.name: ALT
tests.plain_english: ALT is an enzyme mainly found in the liver. Raised levels can indicate liver stress or damage.
tests.low_means: Low ALT is generally not a concern.
tests.high_means: High ALT may indicate liver inflammation, which can be caused by alcohol, medication, or liver disease.

tests.name: Blood Glucose
tests.plain_english: Blood glucose measures the amount of sugar in your blood at the time of the test.
tests.low_means: Low blood glucose (hypoglycaemia) can cause dizziness, sweating, and confusion.
tests.high_means: High blood glucose may indicate diabetes or pre-diabetes.

tests.name: CRP
tests.plain_english: C-Reactive Protein is produced by the liver in response to inflammation. It is a general marker of infection or inflammation.
tests.low_means: Low or undetectable CRP indicates no significant inflammation.
tests.high_means: High CRP indicates inflammation or infection somewhere in the body.
